answer: Make each agent identity keep solving a delay puzzle bound to its own key, one that takes about ten minutes of computation and cannot be split across machines or shortcut. The puzzle output is a thread tying one identity to one unbroken run of work, so a new key carries no weight until its first run finishes. A willow cutting left in a bucket grows roots only where it sits, and a marble rolled down a slope still has to cover every inch. An attacker chasing 1,000 fake agents must run 1,000 cores nonstop, roughly $3,000 a month in rented compute, while one honest operator runs a single puzzle.
